source_files: coverage.csv, sources.json and gaps_by_state.md from the 2026-11-07 case law access survey, and the per-court years in CourtListener's public bulk data of 2026-09-30. The survey opened public court and library web pages and read what they said; it logged in nowhere and used no CourtListener key. Court sites change, so treat every row as a place to start looking.

legend.CAP: Harvard's Caselaw Access Project: a free bulk copy of reported (published) opinions that ends between 2008 and 2019, depending on the state
legend.Scholar: Google Scholar case law (web search only)
legend.JS: needs JavaScript, which the survey's automated check could not run

status.accessible: the survey could open the page
status.partial: only part of it could be read
status.blocked: the survey's automated check was refused, or the site disallows automated readers; it may still open in your own browser
status.unknown: not checked, or the survey could not tell

basis.observed: the survey read the start year on the page
basis.inferred: the survey worked the start year out from what it could see

facts.robots-txt: the site's robots.txt asks automated tools to stay out, so the survey did not read it
facts.needs-script: the opinion lists load with a script, which the survey's automated check could not run
facts.cl-not-in-use: CourtListener lists the court as not in use
facts.cl-historical: CourtListener lists the court as a historical court that has ended
facts.cl-no-new-intake: CourtListener's court record shows no automatic collection of new opinions from this court
facts.govinfo-absent: GovInfo has no opinions from this court
facts.govinfo-stale: GovInfo has stopped receiving opinions from this court
facts.govinfo-elective: GovInfo carries only the opinions a court chooses to send it

legend.cl: CourtListener rows: id (its court id), since and ended (years, from its court record), and with bulk years count, approximate (opinions with approximate dates), earliest and latest (dates, approximate ones left out) and clamp (an earliest year that fell before both the court's start and the Caselaw Access Project's earliest year, raised to the latter; or, with no such project year, a year below 1600 marked as not found)
